How much does AC compressor replacement cost?

A new AC compressor, installed and recharged — what it costs, and what moves the price:

$1,081–$1,463

Parts $836–$1,103 · labor $245–$360 · compressors last 8–10 years

Bay Area: no published metro-specific figure found — the national range is the honest reference.

Why quotes run $750 to $2,000

The compressor
$836–$1,103 shop-supplied. It's three-quarters of the bill — sourcing the part yourself is the biggest lever you've got.
Refrigerant
The system must be evacuated and recharged — by law, not vented. Newer R-1234yf refrigerant costs more than the older R-134a.
Collateral damage
A seized compressor sends metal through the system — then you're also replacing the condenser and flushing everything. Costs jump fast.
Vehicle
Standard sedans land mid-range; European and dual-zone systems run higher. Tight engine bays add labor hours.

What the extra money buys

Used OEM
$100–$205 part

Cheapest route for an older car. Buy only with disclosed donor mileage and capped ports — and always replace the drier with it.

New
$836–$1,103 part

The safe pick on a keeper. Full warranty, no moisture history, no mystery. Remanufactured ($112–$139 part) splits the difference.

Bottom line: the part dominates this bill, so shop the part, not the labor. And whatever you buy, the receiver/drier gets replaced with it — no exceptions.

Common questions

How do I know it's the compressor?

Warm air with the AC on, loud rattling or clicking from the engine bay, or a seized clutch. Get a proper diagnosis — low refrigerant mimics compressor failure.

Can I drive without fixing it?

Yes — a dead compressor doesn't affect drivability. But a leaking system left alone can destroy the compressor, turning a recharge into a replacement.

Can I replace it myself?

Partly. You can buy the part, but refrigerant recovery requires certified equipment — it's illegal to vent it. Most DIYers pay a shop for evacuate-and-recharge.

How long do compressors last?

8–10 years or 60,000–70,000 miles. Leaks, clogs, and moisture in the lines kill them early.

Every car prices differently.
